title: 2023 AMC 12A Problem 15
statement: Usain is walking for exercise by zigzagging across a \(100\)-meter by \(30\)-meter rectangular field, beginning at point \(A\) and ending on the segment \(\overline{BC}.\) He wants to increase the distance walked by zigzagging as shown in the figure below (\(APQRS\)). What angle \(\theta=\angle PAB\) \(=\angle QPC\) \(=\angle RQB=\cdots\) will produce a length that is \(120\) meters? (Do not assume the zigzag path has exactly four segments as shown; there could be more or fewer.)

solutions.text:
Every segment of the zigzag makes angle \(\theta\) with a horizontal side of the field. Therefore a segment of length \(s\) advances \(s\cos\theta\) meters horizontally. This remains true for the last segment even if it ends before crossing the full width of the field.

Adding the horizontal projections over the entire \(120\)-meter path gives \(120\cos\theta=100.\)

Therefore \(\cos\theta=\dfrac56,\) so \(\theta=\arccos\dfrac56.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The horizontal projection of each zigzag segment is its length multiplied by \(\cos\theta\)
Add the horizontal projections of all the segments and compare the \(100\)-meter progress with the \(120\)-meter path
